title: One record of what `sdb-reader ask` prints
description: The command prints a JSON array with one such record per file, or writes one a line with --output (SDW-26). A record says whether a model was asked about the file; where it was, how many sheets the file holds, what was sent, what the model answered, and the answer in the form `read` gives a sheet, so that `diff` can set the two beside each other. A file the request failed for is named on stderr and has no record.

kind.description: What the file is, by the reader's verdict. A model is asked only about a safety-data-sheet: a German one.

asked.description: Whether a model was asked about the file.

reason.description: Why no model was asked. Only where asked is false.

model.description: The model's name at the endpoint.

sheet_count.description: How many safety data sheets the file holds. Each is asked about with a request of its own.

sent.description: Which part of the file's text was sent: from its beginning up to the heading of section 3, or the first pages where no such heading was found. For a file with several sheets, or with a cover page in front of its sheet: before-section-3 where every sheet went up to its own heading of section 3, sheet where at least one went whole. A cover page is never sent.

stage.description: The reading stage the text sent comes from, as extraction_stage() names it.

question.description: A fingerprint of the instructions, which are the same for every file. Answers with another fingerprint are answers to another question.

preset.description: The preset the request's fields come from. Only where --preset named one.

request.description: The fields added to the request: those of the preset, with those of --request-json on top. Only where there were any.

usage.description: What the requests cost in tokens, for a file with several sheets all of them together. Only where the endpoint says.

reading.description: For a file with several sheets the sheets' readings united: the codes of all in the order they first appear, the statements one sheet after the other, each on its line, supplier and date of the first sheet.

answer.description: The model's answer as it gave it. Its keys are the model's; the instructions ask for supplier, hazard_statements, precautionary_statements, supplemental_phrases and revision_date. Only for a file that is one sheet; the answers about several sheets stand under parts.

parts.description: Only for a file with several sheets: what was sent and answered for each, in the file's order.

sent.description: The sheet's text up to its own heading of section 3, or the whole sheet where it has none.

usage.description: What this sheet's request cost in tokens. Only where the endpoint says.

answer.description: The model's answer about this sheet as it gave it.

code.description: What is noted. The same in every language; the codes are those of `read`.

message.description: The sentence, from the message catalog of the language chosen.

reading.description: The model's answer under the names a `read` record's sheet has, as far as a model is asked.

revision_date.description: The date of revision the model named, where the string it named stands in the text sent and is a date; null otherwise.

revision_date_named.description: The string the model named as the date of revision, whether or not it held up.

hazard_codes.description: The codes of the H statements in the model's order; a joined code is one entry.

precautionary_codes.description: The codes of the P statements; a joined code is one entry.

supplemental_codes.description: The codes of the EUH statements, also of one the model listed among the H statements.
